### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you looking for an exciting and fulfilling career implementing the Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA)?The State Water Resources Control Board has an opening for a Senior Environmental Scientist Supervisor in the Office of Sustainable Groundwater Management. The position is located at 1001 I Street, 13th Floor, Sacramento, right in the heart of downtown next to light rail stations and other public transportation The incumbent will help implement the Water Board’s provisions of SGMA. SGMA was enacted to halt groundwater overdraft and bring groundwater basins into balanced levels of pumping and recharge, ideally through local management of groundwater. The Board’s implementation of SGMA will involve supporting local, regional, and statewide efforts and may involve limiting pumping, on a temporary basis, where and when found to be warranted. ### **Job Description and Duties**


Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  

  

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) supervises and directs the work of professional scientific or technical staff and performs the most complex professional scientific office and fieldwork assignments for the Environmental Monitoring Branch's Groundwater Protection Program (GWPP). The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) is responsible for directing employees, addressing employee grievances, and evaluating employee performance.
  

  

The SES Supervisor also:


* Supervises, hires, trains, and evaluates staff assigned to the Environmental Monitoring Branch’s GWPP. Develops operational plans and ensures implementation of program priorities. Responsible for full range of first level supervisory duties; prepares and reviews personnel transactions and documents; participates in sensitive and confidential personnel problems; evaluates and supports staff performance and teamwork to maintain superior quality in completing projects; mentors staff in key scientific skills; identifies training needs; prepares annual performance evaluations; and proactively addresses performance deficiencies utilizing the progressive discipline process.
* Reviews, edits, and writes reports, policies, procedures, and technical publications. Represents the Department and makes presentations to governmental organizations, professional societies, or industry groups. Conducts policy evaluations.
* Conceives, plans, organizes, and supervises the most complex groundwater monitoring studies and oversees research conducted to determine the environmental fate and transport of pesticides. Evaluates study protocols for proper experimental design and statistical analysis, and reviews reports for scientific accuracy and clarity. Participates in the evaluation of collected data and in the development of environmental program policies and procedures based on scientific findings from both internal and external sources.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.


### **Working Conditions**


Employee must have the ability to work in a high\-rise office environment and ability to use a computer monitor, mouse, and keyboard within an 8\-hr day. Employee must be capable of performing field studies and site visits that may involve hiking or climbing in areas with moderate slopes, unpaved surfaces, undeveloped roads, and other areas or structures where studies may be required. The employee must have the ability to conduct fieldwork for long hours under a variety of climatic conditions and, also, operate vehicles on public roadways or travel to remote areas. Travel that includes flying and/or driving on short notice and overnight stays will be required on trips to various field locations and community/board meetings.
  

  

Employee may occasionally be required to wear Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) in order to minimize exposure to hazards. PPE include, but not limited to, gloves, safety glasses, ear plugs, hard hats, coveralls, and tight\-fitting respiratory protective equipment. When respiratory protective equipment is required, the employee must adhere to the fitting requirements stated in DPR’s respiratory protection policy.
  

  

**NOTE:** This position may be eligible for hybrid telework under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria set forth in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location, as indicated on their duty statement, at their own expense.
  

  

Beginning July 1, 2026, it is anticipated the position will be office\-centered and employees will be expected to report to the office at least four days per week.

jobs.title: Emergency Services Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Self\-Help Enterprises (SHE) is seeking a detail\-oriented and analytical professional to join our Emergency Services team. In this role, you will help maintain reliable program data, develop reports and dashboards, identify trends and data\-quality issues, and provide staff with the tools and information needed to monitor services, meet reporting requirements, and make informed decisions. **Responsibilities:**


In this position, you may:

* Collect, organize, maintain, and analyze program and participant data across departmental databases and systems, ensuring accuracy, consistency, completeness, and accessibility.
* Design, develop, and maintain databases, data integrations, ETL processes, and other data systems that support program operations, reporting, and analysis.
* Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, and data\-visualization tools using platforms such as Power BI and Excel to communicate program performance and outcomes.
* Conduct routine and comprehensive data audits to identify missing information, inaccurate fields, incorrect statuses, and other record\-keeping gaps; work with program staff to correct issues and prevent recurrence.
* Establish and support data\-quality assurance and governance practices that promote the accuracy, integrity, consistency, and appropriate security of departmental data.
* Extract and analyze program data to identify trends, service gaps, risks, and opportunities for improvement, and communicate findings clearly to staff and leadership.
* Conduct spatial and GIS analysis using ArcGIS to support program planning, service delivery, regulatory compliance, and strategic decision\-making.
* Prepare data and reports in accordance with grant, contract, funder, and regulatory requirements, including applicable state and federal reporting standards.
* Support the development of key performance indicators, outcome measures, forecasting analyses, and other evaluation tools used to assess and strengthen departmental programs.
* Develop and implement automated solutions for recurring data, workflow, and reporting processes using tools such as Power Automate and Power Apps.
* Support data projects involving system migrations, integrations, APIs, process improvements, and implementing new data tools and solutions.
* Develop and maintain data dictionaries, user guides, system documentation, procedures, and training materials to promote consistent data practices and understanding across the department.
* Provide technical assistance and troubleshoot data discrepancies, reporting challenges, and system issues, coordinating or escalating more complex matters when needed.
* Develop and deliver training sessions and workshops to help staff use departmental data systems, reports, dashboards, and other tools effectively.
* Collaborate with program staff, department leadership, community partners, funding agencies, and other stakeholders to identify data needs and develop practical solutions.
* Provide data\-informed recommendations and technical guidance to support departmental planning, program evaluation, compliance, and decision\-making.

 **Must Haves**


The ideal candidate will bring a combination of the following:

* Experience collecting, maintaining, validating, analyzing, or reporting data.
* Strong attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy and integrity.
* Experience using Excel and data\-visualization or reporting tools such as Power BI.
* Ability to identify data discrepancies, investigate their causes, and develop practical solutions.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and problem\-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and data projects in a fast\-paced environment.
* Ability to explain data, systems, and technical concepts clearly to nontechnical audiences.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with program staff, leadership, partners, and funding agencies.
* Experience with databases, ETL processes, ArcGIS, Power Automate, Power Apps, APIs, or data\-governance practices is desirable and may be required for the higher\-level classifications.
* Knowledge of grant, contract, regulatory, state, or federal reporting requirements is highly desirable.

Are you interested in furthering the State's commitment to reduce climate change? Would you like to be a part a new team evaluating and enforcing the State's landmark legislation for climate change through organics collection and recycling? Do you have experience in evaluating and verifying compliance with environmental laws? Are you motivated about the opportunity to oversee and accomplish compliance at the local level to achieve statewide environmental goals?

### **Job Description and Duties**


Under the general direction of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory). The incumbent is an interdisciplinary team member on Project Development Teams (PDT) performing the most complex tasks to facilitate timely delivery of transportation projects within the coastal zone. The incumbent shall lead, with minimal supervision, data analysis, document preparation and application preparation for addressing coastal resources as part of the California Coastal Act and Coastal Zone Management Act. The incumbent shall facilitate State and Local coastal permit coordination, obtain Coastal Development Permits, waivers, exclusions and represent North Region Environmental at coordination meetings and public hearings with coastal permitting agencies while closely tracking and reporting on the status of permits and complex mitigation packages.
  

  

The incumbent must stay informed of changes related to environmental laws, local coastal plans and policies, lead PDT’s in the applicability of such changes, existing law, plans and policies, and provide guidance and direction to PDT’s to ensure development of appropriate mitigation measures relative to coastal resource impacts such as Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Areas, wetlands, water quality, public access, historic resources, cultural resources, critical viewsheds, and coastal hazards. Ensure and review inclusion of Sea Level Rise analysis and other Climate Adaptions Strategies, and associated avoidance, minimization, and mitigation measures. The incumbent is responsible for leading coordination efforts to manage the cost, scope and schedule of transportation projects within the coastal zone to ensure the Environmental Program meets its project delivery commitments under the Annual Delivery Plan (ADP) and the Contract for Delivery (CFD).

jobs.title: Community Services Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Why Join Team SB**
--------------------

  

  

**Are you seeking professional growth and development?**  

**Consider joining the City of San Bernardino's Parks, Recreation, \& Community Services Department as** **a** ***Community Services Program Coordin******ator*** **for the Aquatics Division****!** **About the City:**
As a future member of our team, you’ll be joining a city with deep roots, cultural diversity, and exciting momentum. Located in the heart of Southern California’s Inland Empire, San Bernardino is the county seat and largest city in San Bernardino County, home to more than 222,000 residents. Its rich history — shaped by Native American, Mexican, and Spanish influences — continues to inspire the city’s evolving identity.
San Bernardino offers access to major transit corridors, natural beauty, and a wide range of housing and lifestyle options. It’s a place where public service careers are supported by a strong sense of community and purpose — and where motivated professionals can grow, contribute, and be part of something meaningful.

**About the Position:**  

The Aquatics Coordinator is responsible for the day\-to\-day operation and overall oversight of aquatic facilities, including staff scheduling, training, and supervision of lifeguard, swim instructors, and frontline staff. This role ensures a safe, well\-maintained, and welcoming environment for all patrons while managing the aquatics budget, supplies, marketing presence, and staff training and performance evaluations. Work schedule may require evenings, weekends, and holidays based on facility programming needs. On\-call availability for emergencies may be required. **Duties \& Responsibilities****:** **Staff Management \& Training*** Recruit, hire, train, schedule, and supervise lifeguards, swim instructors, and other aquatics staff.
* Develop and maintain staff work schedules to ensure adequate coverage during all hours of facility operation.
* Conduct regular in\-service trainings, lifeguard skill audits, and emergency response drills.
* Perform annual staff performance evaluations and provide ongoing coaching and feedback.
* Ensure all staff certifications (lifeguard, CPR/AED, First Aid, Water Safety Instructor, Title 22 etc.) remain current.
* Address staff performance issues, conduct disciplinary actions when necessary, and maintain accurate personnel records.

 **Facility Oversight*** Provide overall oversight of the aquatic facility, including pool operations, safety protocols, and cleanliness standards.
* Monitor water chemistry and coordinate with maintenance staff to ensure compliance with local health and safety codes.
* Conduct routine facility inspections and address safety hazards promptly.
* Develop, implement, and enforce facility policies, rules, and emergency action plans.
* Serve as the primary point of contact during emergencies and incidents, completing and processing required incident reports.

 **Customer Service \& Communication*** Model and reinforce excellent customer service techniques among staff and patrons.

This position supports compliance with requirements established by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), including the Division of Licensing and the Division of Hydropower Administration and Compliance (DHAC), as well as internal programmatic systems and processes. **Why Join Team SB**
--------------------

  

  

**Are you seeking professional growth and development?**  

**Consider joining the City of San Bernardino's Parks, Recreation, \& Community Services Department as** **a** ***Community Services Program Coordin******ator*** **for the Aquatics Division****!** **About the City:**
As a future member of our team, you’ll be joining a city with deep roots, cultural diversity, and exciting momentum. Located in the heart of Southern California’s Inland Empire, San Bernardino is the county seat and largest city in San Bernardino County, home to more than 222,000 residents. Its rich history — shaped by Native American, Mexican, and Spanish influences — continues to inspire the city’s evolving identity.
San Bernardino offers access to major transit corridors, natural beauty, and a wide range of housing and lifestyle options. It’s a place where public service careers are supported by a strong sense of community and purpose — and where motivated professionals can grow, contribute, and be part of something meaningful.

**About the Position:**  

The Aquatics Coordinator is responsible for the day\-to\-day operation and overall oversight of aquatic facilities, including staff scheduling, training, and supervision of lifeguard, swim instructors, and frontline staff. This role ensures a safe, well\-maintained, and welcoming environment for all patrons while managing the aquatics budget, supplies, marketing presence, and staff training and performance evaluations. Work schedule may require evenings, weekends, and holidays based on facility programming needs. On\-call availability for emergencies may be required. **Duties \& Responsibilities****:** **Staff Management \& Training*** Recruit, hire, train, schedule, and supervise lifeguards, swim instructors, and other aquatics staff.
* Develop and maintain staff work schedules to ensure adequate coverage during all hours of facility operation.
* Conduct regular in\-service trainings, lifeguard skill audits, and emergency response drills.
* Perform annual staff performance evaluations and provide ongoing coaching and feedback.
* Ensure all staff certifications (lifeguard, CPR/AED, First Aid, Water Safety Instructor, Title 22 etc.) remain current.
* Address staff performance issues, conduct disciplinary actions when necessary, and maintain accurate personnel records.

 **Facility Oversight*** Provide overall oversight of the aquatic facility, including pool operations, safety protocols, and cleanliness standards.
* Monitor water chemistry and coordinate with maintenance staff to ensure compliance with local health and safety codes.
* Conduct routine facility inspections and address safety hazards promptly.
* Develop, implement, and enforce facility policies, rules, and emergency action plans.
* Serve as the primary point of contact during emergencies and incidents, completing and processing required incident reports.

 **Customer Service \& Communication*** Model and reinforce excellent customer service techniques among staff and patrons.
* Respond to patron inquiries, concerns, and complaints in a professional and timely manner.
* Communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with staff, patrons, management, and outside agencies.
* Prepare written reports, memos, and correspondence as needed.

 **Marketing \& Social Media*** Create engaging and relevant social media content to promote aquatic programs, classes, and events.
* Collaborate with marketing staff to increase community awareness and program enrollment.
* Maintain accurate and up\-to\-date program information across digital and print platforms.

 **Budget \& Purchasing*** Create, manage, and oversee the annual aquatics budget.
* Monitor expenditures and revenue to ensure fiscal responsibility.
* Purchase necessary aquatic supplies, equipment, and safety gear within budgetary guidelines.
* Maintain accurate inventory records and coordinate equipment repairs/replacements as needed.

 **Program Development*** Plan, implement, and evaluate swim lessons, aquatic fitness classes, and special events.
* Monitor program enrollment and adjust offerings to meet community needs and demand.
* Ensure programs align with organizational goals and safety standards.
  


**What You'll Be Doing Here**
-----------------------------


**The Ideal Candidate:**  

The ideal candidate will be an experienced, safety\-focused aquatics professional with strong leadership and program\-management skills. They will have experience supervising and developing aquatics staff, coordinating facility operations, and ensuring compliance with applicable health and safety standards. The successful candidate will be organized, approachable, and able to remain calm and make sound decisions during emergencies.


They will also possess excellent customer service and communication skills, along with experience managing budgets, supplies, schedules, and aquatic programs. The ideal candidate will take initiative, manage competing priorities effectively, and foster positive working relationships with employees, patrons, City departments, and community partners.

**Position Description**
------------------------


**Check out what the team is up to, and what they have to offer!**


https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/cd418c7ce7d846618cf14d09da16ad50


The Program Coordinator reports to the FERC License Program Manager and provides program coordination and support for the FERC License Program. This position supports the successful delivery of major programs and projects associated with ongoing FERC license compliance, as well as upcoming FERC relicensing, surrender, and transfer activities for Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric projects.


This position supports compliance with requirements established by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), including the Division of Licensing and the Division of Hydropower Administration and Compliance (DHAC), as well as internal programmatic systems and processes. The Program Coordinator assists with tracking license implementation activities, interim and formal schedules, and program milestones to support timely and compliant execution of FERC license requirements. Major tasks include developing and maintaining schedules, budgets, tracking tools, program documentation, reporting, and internal and external communications as well as identification and escalation of issues, risks, and emerging concerns.


The position supports Tacoma Power’s mission to create clean, reliable, and marketable energy while ensuring responsible stewardship of natural and cultural resources. Program activities span a broad range of resource areas, including fish and wildlife, forestry, land management, recreation, cultural resources, instream flows, water quality, and reservoir management.


The Program Coordinator plays an integral role in supporting the FERC Licensing Program and ensuring the current and future goals and obligations associated with Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric project licenses are accomplished in a coordinated, timely, and compliant manner. The position works collaboratively across programs and disciplines within Tacoma Power to align FERC licensing and compliance activities with related operational, environmental, regulatory, and resource stewardship efforts.  

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Coordinate FERC Licensing Program activities** by serving as a member of the FERC Licensing Core Team and supporting coordination across relicensing, license surrender, transfer, and compliance efforts. Facilitate action\-item tracking, decision documentation, communications, and alignment of critical program activities.
* **Develop and maintain program controls and tracking systems** for FERC licensing and compliance activities, including scopes, schedules, budgets, critical paths, milestones, resource availability, risks, action items, and other program performance measures. Provide timely information and reporting to support program management and decision\-making.
* **Coordinate project teams and advisory groups** supporting Tacoma Power’s hydroelectric licenses by facilitating communication, accountability, and alignment among internal teams, consultants, contractors, agencies, and stakeholders. Identify emerging issues and support timely escalation and resolution of risks affecting program objectives.
* **Support FERC license compliance and regulatory requirements** for Tacoma Power’s four hydroelectric projects by monitoring license obligations, reporting requirements, payments, FERC exhibits, agency and stakeholder commitments, and other compliance activities. Track license requirements and deadlines to support timely completion and reduce regulatory risk.
* **Coordinate meetings, communications, and program materials** for senior management, internal and external teams, advisory groups, regulatory agencies, and stakeholders. Develop agendas, presentations, briefing materials, action\-item records, and decision documentation to support effective program communication and governance.
* **Support contracts, task orders, submittals, and program documentation** associated with FERC licensing, relicensing, surrender, transfer, and compliance activities. Coordinate with internal records and information management resources to maintain accurate, accessible, and appropriately controlled program documentation and ensure required FERC submittals are completed and filed on schedule.
* **Promote continuous improvement and professional development** by identifying opportunities to improve program coordination, tracking, reporting, and information management processes; coordinating across related utility functions; and maintaining knowledge of FERC licensing and compliance practices through relevant training, conferences, and professional development.

Bachelor's degree in planning, engineering, architecture, project management or directly related field such as environmental science

**Posted:** 09/15/2026  

  

  

  

**SUMMARY OF JOB DESCRIPTION:**


As a member of CAPE’s Technical Services Organization, the GIS Analyst is responsible for ensuring that all geospatial project activities meet contractual, legal and regulatory requirements resulting in accurate and legally defensible data and project execution. The GIS Analyst is responsible for supporting the planning and execution of all project and proposal activities related to GIS, remote sensing, and/or data management. The ideal candidate will have experience in the environmental/remediation sector and demonstrated ability to drive efficient high\-volume production of maps, charts, and figures. This position will work closely with various teams to support projects, proposals, and business development opportunities to achieve profit goals and excellent client satisfaction in alignment with the Mission, Vision and Values of CAPE.


Responsibilities:


* Use and update GIS libraries, Geodatabases, and project Map Packages
* Support GIS projects, schedules and development of standards and libraries
* Ensure each deliverable sent to an outside client has been produced and reviewed in accordance with established SOPs
* Ensure timely and appropriate generation, collection, dissemination, storage, and ultimate disposition of project information

**SALARY:**
  

$65,000 \- $80,000 annually, commensurate with experience and qualifications.


**TRAVEL:**
  

Up to 1\-2 times per year for technical field support.


**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**


* B.A, B.S, or M.S in Geology, Geography, Environmental Science, GIS, or related field.
* Two years of experience using ArcGIS or other geospatial software to generate unique maps and visualize datasets for technical reports.
* Two years of experience in an environmental, engineering, or science field analyzing and visualizing complex project datasets.
* Demonstrated skill with ArcGIS Pro software.
  

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**


* B.S or M.S in Geology, Geography, Environmental Science, GIS, or related field.
* Minimum of 2\-5 years in a similar role, preference for candidates with experience in the environmental industry serving DoD clients.
* Proficiency in MS Access and SQL relational database management/administration.
* Proficiency in programming in SQL, VBA, and/or Python.
  

**WHY CAPE?**


For 35 years, CAPE has delivered construction and environmental remediation solutions to governmental and private organizations nationwide. Our projects are high\-profile environmental remediation projects involving cleanup of contaminated soil, groundwater, and sediment. The culture of our company is one of working together to achieve our clients’ objectives, company goals, and employees’ professional goals, and is succinctly and accurately defined as “We, Not Me” behavior. To ensure long\-term, sustainable growth, we tailor our 3\-year vision to be ahead of our industry in delivering our projects, align with our clients and team partners to improve our existing market share, and develop new services to support smart growth.


CAPE offers competitive benefits including Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, life insurance, ADP retirement savings plan including both traditional and Roth 401(k) with up to 4% match and lowest in class fees, health savings account (HSA) with investment option, flexible spending account (FSA), paid annual leave, paid maternity/paternity leave, and tuition reimbursement. CAPE also offers staff several other voluntary benefits options, as well as the option to work from home.


CAPE is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. We invite all qualified applicants to apply to our open positions.


**Communication**


Any communication regarding this position will come from an email address ending in cape\-inc.com. Scammers may try to imitate our HR team.
